name: TextField
summary: Single-line text entry with a visible label, optional description and an error message that screen readers announce. Not for multi-line text (TextArea), choosing from options (Select, ComboBox) or dates (DateField).

pattern.name: Native text input — no APG widget pattern; semantics come from <input> + <label>. Follows the WAI Forms tutorial for labels, instructions and error identification.

label.requiredWhen: aria-label is not given. A visible label is the default; the type union refuses a field with neither.
label.intent: The accessible name AND the visible label. Rendered as a real <label> bound by React Aria; clicking it focuses the input.

aria-label.requiredWhen: label is omitted (e.g. the Today quick-add, where the field is the whole row and a visible label would be noise).
aria-label.intent: Name without a visible label. Use sparingly: 2.4.6 and 3.3.2 are easier to meet with a visible label.

description.intent: Help text under the field, linked by aria-describedby. Format hints go here, never in placeholder.

errorMessage.intent: Shown when isInvalid. Present in the DOM before it becomes visible, so aria-invalid + aria-describedby announce it the moment the state flips (docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md § Inputs).

isInvalid.intent: Sets aria-invalid and the invalid style. The field never decides validity itself; the form or pattern does, so the same rule can run on submit and on server response.

isRequired.intent: Sets aria-required and shows the required marker next to the label. Native HTML required is NOT used, so the browser's own bubble never competes with our error message.

isDisabled.intent: Removes from tab order and from form submission. Prefer isReadOnly when the value still matters.

isReadOnly.intent: Focusable, selectable, copyable, not editable; still submitted. Use for values the user must be able to read and copy but not change.

onChange.intent: Fires with the string, not the event (React Aria convention; same signature across all Inputs).

type.intent: Native input type: drives the mobile keyboard, browser autofill and password managers. Not 'number' — use NumberField when it exists.

inputMode.intent: Mobile keyboard override when type alone is wrong (e.g. type=text with inputMode=numeric for a postcode).

autoComplete.intent: HTML autocomplete token (e.g. 'email', 'given-name', 'organization'). Required for personal-data fields: WCAG 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose.

name.intent: Form field name for native submission.

placeholder.intent: Example value only, in muted text. Never the label, never the instructions: it disappears on first keystroke and fails contrast by design.

size.intent: Field heights 40 / 44 px (specs/HANDOFF.md: inputs 40 desktop, 44 phone). lg is the touch default. No sm: a 32 px text field fails the 44 px touch guidance and is rarely right for text entry.

isFullWidth.intent: Stretches to the container's inline size; typical in forms and the quick-add row.

iconStart.intent: Decorative leading icon inside the field (search, @). aria-hidden applied automatically; it never carries meaning.

kbdHint.intent: Trailing <kbd> showing the shortcut that focuses this field (the handoff's 'N' for quick-add). aria-hidden: the shortcut is documented in the list header, not announced per field.

autoFocus.intent: Focus on mount. Only for the single primary field of a view (quick-add); never on a field below the fold.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to / from the input. The label, description, error and kbd hint are never tab stops.
Edits the value; onChange fires with the string. Native editing keys (Home/End, Shift+Arrow, ⌘A, ⌘Z) are untouched.
Not handled by the field. Inside a <form> it submits natively; a pattern (quick-add) may listen, but the field never calls preventDefault on it.
Not handled by the field. The quick-add pattern clears on Escape; a Dialog closes on it. The field must not stop propagation, or those break.

a11y.name: From the visible label (a real <label for>, via React Aria's Label), or from aria-label when label is omitted — the type union requires one of the two.
a11y.announcements: isInvalid → aria-invalid="true"; aria-describedby lists description then error, so the error is read on focus and on the state change. isRequired → aria-required="true" plus a visible marker. isReadOnly → aria-readonly="true"; the value is still read.
a11y.targetSize: md 40×40 (meets 2.5.8 AA minimum 24; desktop default per handoff), lg 44 (touch). The whole field box is the target, not just the text.

rules: A visible label is the default. placeholder is never the label and never the instructions — it vanishes on the first keystroke and its muted colour is below AA by design (3.3.2, 2.4.6).
The error message is in the DOM before it is visible (hidden with the visually-hidden utility, not display:none), so flipping isInvalid announces it immediately through aria-describedby (3.3.1).
Invalid is never colour-only: the border changes AND the error text appears AND aria-invalid is set. Colour-blind users and screen-reader users get the same information (1.4.1).
The field never calls preventDefault or stopPropagation on Enter or Escape. Quick-add (Enter adds, Esc clears) and Dialog (Esc closes) own those keys at the pattern level.

Global shortcuts (J/K/D/S/N/F) are the app's responsibility to suppress inside editable elements: the app's handler checks event.target.isContentEditable || tagName in INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT. The field does not need to know about them.
Personal-data fields set autoComplete (email, name, organization, …): WCAG 1.3.5 and the single biggest usability win on mobile.
Focus ring is outline + outline-offset on the field box, never box-shadow alone (clipped by overflow, ignored in forced-colors). Same recipe as Button.
In forced-colors mode keep a visible border (FieldText / Highlight) so the field box is visible in Windows High Contrast.
The kbd hint is aria-hidden and sits inside the field box on the trailing edge; it must not shrink the editable area below 40 px or overlap the value.
Heights: md = size.target.lg (40 px), lg = size.target.touch (44 px) — the same two tokens Button md / lg use, so a field and its button align in a row (ADR-021).

properties.Label: label
properties.Error: errorMessage (boolean show + text; visible only when State = invalid)

examples.title: Email with description
examples.code: <TextField label="Email" type="email" autoComplete="email" description="We only use this for the digest." />

examples.title: Invalid with error
examples.code: <TextField label="Salary floor" inputMode="numeric" isInvalid errorMessage="Enter a number, e.g. 120000" />

examples.title: Quick-add row (no visible label)
examples.code: <TextField aria-label="Add an action" placeholder="Email Priya @Orbit tomorrow 10am" kbdHint="N" isFullWidth autoFocus />
